result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You were in hospital with pneumonia (a lung illness). Treatment at home did not make it better. Your oxygen levels were low (hypoxia).

The doctors think the cause may be a virus. They call it atypical pneumonia. The lung doctor was not sure of the exact cause. He thought a virus was the most likely.

Your first x-ray showed some mild patchy marks (infiltrates). A CT scan found no specific focal pathology.

Doctors also think you may have mild adrenal insufficiency. This may be from the stress of the pneumonia, because you take prednisone all the time. This is not certain.

You also have rheumatoid arthritis. Methotrexate is known to cause pneumonitis on some occasions.

Your fever broke 18 hours before you left hospital. Your oxygen levels got better. Your strength got better too.

One test is not back yet. This is the C. difficile toxin test. The result is pending. The letter does not say who will tell you the result.

## What you need to do
1. Finish your azithromycin. You have two pills left at home.
2. Keep taking prednisone at the higher dose of 20 mg.
3. See Dr. X in two to three days.

## Dates and medicines
- Follow-up with Dr. X: in two to three days.
- Azithromycin: keep taking it until it is finished. The letter gives no dose.
- Prednisone: 20 mg per day. Before, it was 5 mg per day. Keep the higher dose.
- Methotrexate: 20 mg every week. It was held this past Friday. The hospital team will ask your rheumatologist whether to continue it. That decision is still waiting.
- Remicade: every eight weeks. Your last dose was in June.
- Rocephin (ceftriaxone): you had it by IV in hospital. Before hospital it was 1 g daily, starting three days before you were admitted. The letter does not say what happens with it after you leave.
- Avelox: you had a reaction to it. It was stopped and changed to Augmentin.
- Augmentin: it caused loose stools. It was stopped and changed to Rocephin and azithromycin.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- When will I get the C. difficile test result, and who will tell me?
- What does adrenal insufficiency mean for me?
- Should I take methotrexate again? When will I know?
- What happens with the Rocephin now?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
